model.name: Headline (average of the two)
model.description: The average of two models that read different indicators: a regression on GDP's last value and a few activity indicators, and a factor model on a wider set. The weights are equal because we cannot yet say which model is better.

members.name: Regression on activity indicators
members.description: GDP growth regressed on its own last value and the quarterly growth of Index of Industrial Production - General Index, Index of Core Industries (ICI) and Foreign Exchange Reserves - Total. A guard drops any indicator that nearly duplicates a better one.
indicators: Index of Industrial Production - General Index

members.name: Factor model
members.description: 2 common trends found in 17 monthly indicators by principal components, averaged to quarters. GDP growth is regressed on them and on its own last value.
indicators: Index of Industrial Production - General Index

indicatorsReporting: Index of Industrial Production - General Index

caveats: The headline averages two models: a regression on GDP's last value and 3 activity indicators, and a factor model on 17 indicators. In ordinary quarters the headline has been closer to the first print than the AR(1) benchmark, but only narrowly, so luck could still explain it. The live record is the clean test.
The range is where past first prints fell around the headline in ordinary conditions, with the COVID years left out. The tail-risk range allows for a miss as large as 2020's.
The track record is a backtest. Each estimate was made a week before the first print, using only data released before it but with today's revised values. Live runs are listed separately.

The headline reads indicators in Industry, Construction and investment, Household consumption, Government, External sector, Money, credit and financial conditions and Prices. It reads nothing in Services, Agriculture and the rural economy and Labour.
Each indicator's contribution is a simple projection. What it leaves out, mainly GDP's own persistence and the factors' dynamics, is shown as carried forward.
The training sample includes the 2020 to 2021 COVID quarters, with no adjustment.

evaluation.basis: backtest: pseudo-real-time, first prints, quarters from 2012-13 Q3

selection.definition: Quarters starting through Oct 2019, before COVID.

confirmation.definition: Quarters starting from Jul 2022, after the COVID base effects.

ordinary.definition: Selection and confirmation together: everything outside the COVID window (quarters starting Jan 2020 to Oct 2021) and the base-effect quarters through Apr 2022. Our main claims refer to this sample.

exCovid.definition: Everything outside the COVID window. It adds the two 2022 base-effect quarters, where the AR(1) benchmark missed badly, so models look better here than on ordinary quarters.

gaps.missing: Kharif and rabi sowing and output estimates, monsoon rainfall, tractor and fertiliser sales
gaps.why: Roughly a sixth of GVA, and neither model reads an indicator for it
gaps.candidateSource: Ministry of Agriculture, IMD, FADA and SIAM monthly releases

gaps.missing: Services PMI, air passenger traffic, railway freight and passenger earnings, FASTag toll collections
gaps.why: Over half of GVA. We hold only one bank-credit series and GST for it
gaps.candidateSource: S&P Global PMI, DGCA, Indian Railways, NHAI

gaps.missing: Passenger-vehicle and two-wheeler sales, UPI transaction value and volume, FMCG volumes
gaps.why: Private consumption is the largest part of demand. Fuel use is the only direct measure we hold
gaps.candidateSource: SIAM and FADA, NPCI (a timely, real-time series), company and industry releases

gaps.why: Investment demand. The IIP capital-goods index is in files we hold but is not used yet
gaps.candidateSource: MoSPI IIP use-based tables (held), Tradestat commodity detail (held, when the site restores it)

gaps.missing: The level of merchandise exports, services exports
gaps.why: We hold only the export-import ratio, not the level of exports. Exports are in the Tradestat reports we already have

gaps.missing: Manufacturing PMI and RBI business and consumer surveys
gaps.why: Surveys lead activity and come out within days of the month end

gaps.missing: EPFO payroll additions, MGNREGA work demand
gaps.why: Our only labour series are urban and quarterly, from 2018

coverage.note: Quarterly shortlisted series (house prices, GFCF, the current account, PLFS) appear here but not in `drivers` or `signals`, which are monthly or finer.
